name: Electoral system
description: How votes turn into results. Required on every contest, since a result means nothing without it. 40% wins outright under first-past-the-post, forces a runoff under a two-round system, and earns only a share of seats under a party list. Naming the system lets this profile work in any country.

hasDefinedTerm.name: First past the post
hasDefinedTerm.description: One seat. Most votes wins. No majority needed.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Block vote
hasDefinedTerm.description: Several seats. Each voter gets as many votes as there are seats. The highest totals win.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Two-round
hasDefinedTerm.description: A second round between the leading candidates if no one clears the threshold in the first round.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Party-list proportional
hasDefinedTerm.description: Seats go to parties in proportion to their share of the vote.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Single transferable vote
hasDefinedTerm.description: Several seats, ranked ballots. Extra and eliminated votes transfer to other candidates.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Mixed-member proportional
hasDefinedTerm.description: Some seats come from constituencies, and list seats top up the total to make it proportional.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Parallel or mixed
hasDefinedTerm.description: Constituency seats and list seats are counted separately, with no top-up between them.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Ranked choice (instant runoff)
hasDefinedTerm.description: One seat, ranked ballots. The last-place candidate is eliminated and their votes transfer until someone has a majority.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Approval
hasDefinedTerm.description: Voters can approve as many candidates as they like. Most approvals wins.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Indirect
hasDefinedTerm.description: Chosen by an electoral college or a sitting body instead of directly by voters.
